{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0182cjDgoTDyfTq48qXmyJzr","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Careexpand LLC — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: https://www.careexpand.com\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Careexpand LLC is a small health IT company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Plano/Dallas, Texas. The company has approximately 1–10 employees (per ZoomInfo) and a listed team of about 16 people on their website, including CEO Javier Vinals, CTO Pablo Vinals, and Chief Software Strategist Ameya Parab. The company secured initial funding in 2018, launched a beta in 2019, and released a \"full-suite version with integrated modules\" in 2024. They received ONC certification in April 2025, making them a very recently certified product.\n     9→\n    10→Careexpand positions itself as \"the operating system for continuity of care\" — a cloud-based SaaS platform integrating EHR, telemedicine, care coordination, and practice management. They market to individual doctors, small clinics, healthcare payers, and large health systems. The website claims 20,000+ registered users, though this likely refers to patient portal registrations rather than clinical users. The platform operates in English and Spanish.\n    11→\n    12→The company is a startup-stage vendor with no presence on major review aggregator sites (G2, Capterra, GetApp). There are no identifiable third-party reviews. No notable customers or case studies were found beyond generic testimonial quotes on the vendor's website. There is no evidence of acquisitions, mergers, or white-labeling. The product appears to be a proprietary, ground-up build.\n    13→\n    14→## Product: Careexpand\n    15→\n    16→CHPL IDs: 11625 (15.04.04.3226.Care.24.00.1.250422)\n    17→\n    18→### What It Is\n    19→\n    20→Careexpand is a cloud-based, all-in-one healthcare platform combining EHR, telemedicine, remote patient monitoring (RPM), care coordination, and practice management. The certified module covers the full platform — it is not a component of a larger product. The product is offered in three pricing tiers that reflect escalating functionality:\n    21→\n    22→1. **Telemedicine Plan** ($49/mo per provider) — Video/phone consultations, basic scheduling\n    23→2. **Continuity of Care Plan** ($149/mo per provider) — Adds care coordination, referral management, follow-up protocols\n    24→3. **Full Practice Management Plan** ($249/mo per provider) — Adds EHR, e-prescribing, lab orders, billing, reporting, CQMs\n    25→\n    26→An additional Change Healthcare/Optum integration is available for $65/mo per provider for orders.\n    27→\n    28→### Users & Market\n    29→\n    30→**Intended users** (per CHPL): Providers, FNPs, Clinicians.\n    31→\n    32→**Target settings**: Individual doctors, small clinics, multi-provider groups, and (aspirationally) larger health systems and payer organizations. The enterprise page targets health systems, payers, provider networks, and retail/DTC brands — though it's unclear how many enterprise clients they actually serve.\n    33→\n    34→**Market position**: Very small, startup-stage vendor. No identifiable market share data. Not listed on KLAS, G2, Capterra, or other review platforms. The 20,000+ users figure on the website likely includes patient accounts, not just clinical users.\n    35→\n    36→**Clinical settings**: Appears focused on ambulatory/outpatient care, with emphasis on primary care, chronic disease management (diabetes, hypertension), and urgent care. No evidence of inpatient, surgical, behavioral health, or specialty-specific modules.\n    37→\n    38→### Modules & Functionality\n    39→\n    40→Based on vendor website and mandatory disclosures page:\n    41→\n    42→**Electronic Health Records (EHR)**\n    43→- Patient demographics management (certified (a)(5))\n    44→- Clinical documentation with AI-assisted automated coding and metatags\n    45→- Problem lists, medication lists, allergy lists (implied by CCDA/transitions of care certification)\n    46→- Implantable device tracking (certified (a)(14))\n    47→- CPOE for The company has approximately 1–10 employees (per ZoomInfo) and a listed team of about 16 people on their website, including CEO Javier Vinals, CTO Pablo Vinals, and Chief Software Strategist Ameya Parab. The company secured initial funding in 2018, launched a beta in 2019, and released a \"full-suite version with integrated modules\" in 2024. They received ONC certification in April 2025, making them a very recently certified product.\n\nCareexpand positions itself as \"the operating system for continuity of care\" — a cloud-based SaaS platform integrating EHR, telemedicine, care coordination, and practice management. They market to individual doctors, small clinics, healthcare payers, and large health systems. The website claims 20,000+ registered users, though this likely refers to patient portal registrations rather than clinical users. There is no evidence of acquisitions, mergers, or white-labeling. The product appears to be a proprietary, ground-up build.\n\n## Product: Careexpand\n\nCHPL IDs: 11625 (15.04.04.3226.Care.24.00.1.250422)\n\n### What It Is\n\nCareexpand is a cloud-based, all-in-one healthcare platform combining EHR, telemedicine, remote patient monitoring (RPM), care coordination, and practice management. The certified module covers the full platform — it is not a component of a larger product. The product is offered in three pricing tiers that reflect escalating functionality:\n\n1. **Telemedicine Plan** ($49/mo per provider) — Video/phone consultations, basic scheduling\n2. **Continuity of Care Plan** ($149/mo per provider) — Adds care coordination, referral management, follow-up protocols\n3. **Full Practice Management Plan** ($249/mo per provider) — Adds EHR, e-prescribing, lab orders, billing, reporting, CQMs\n\nAn additional Change Healthcare/Optum integration is available for $65/mo per provider for orders.\n\n### Users & Market\n\n**Intended users** (per CHPL): Providers, FNPs, Clinicians.\n\n**Target settings**: Individual doctors, small clinics, multi-provider groups, and (aspirationally) larger health systems and payer organizations. The enterprise page targets health systems, payers, provider networks, and retail/DTC brands — though it's unclear how many enterprise clients they actually serve.\n\n**Market position**: Very small, startup-stage vendor. No identifiable market share data. Not listed on KLAS, G2, Capterra, or other review platforms. The 20,000+ users figure on the website likely includes patient accounts, not just clinical users.\n\n**Clinical settings**: Appears focused on ambulatory/outpatient care, with emphasis on primary care, chronic disease management (diabetes, hypertension), and urgent care. No evidence of inpatient, surgical, behavioral health, or specialty-specific modules.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on vendor website and mandatory disclosures page:\n\n**Electronic Health Records (EHR)**\n- Patient demographics management (certified (a)(5))\n- Clinical documentation with AI-assisted automated coding and metatags\n- Problem lists, medication lists, allergy lists (implied by CCDA/transitions of care certification)\n- Implantable device tracking (certified (a)(14))\n- CPOE for medications (certified (a)(1))\n- Ultra-customizable interface for specialists and family medicine\n\n**E-Prescribing & Lab Orders**\n- AI-assisted electronic prescribing\n- Pre-configured protocols for common conditions (diabetes, hypertension)\n- Lab order integration\n- Change Healthcare/Optum integration for orders ($65/mo add-on)\n\n**Telemedicine**\n- Video and phone consultations\n- Virtual waiting rooms\n- Multi-channel messaging\n- Patient portal with web/mobile access\n\n**Care Coordination & Continuity of Care**\n- Automated referral suggestions based on patient history and physician patterns\n- Follow-up protocol recommendations\n- Care plan management (certified (b)(11))\n- Transitions of care / C-CDA exchange (certified (b)(1))\n- Direct messaging for health information exchange (certified (h)(1))\n\n**Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM)**\n- Device delivery and configuration (mentioned but specifics not detailed)\n- Clinical monitoring and alerts\n- Continuous tracking for chronic conditions (diabetes, hypertension, heart disease mentioned)\n- Specific devices and metrics not enumerated on the website\n\n**Scheduling & Patient Engagement**\n- Unified scheduling and workflow calendar (in-person and remote)\n- Automated appointment reminders\n- Patient portal with health information access\n- Personalized engagement campaigns\n\n**Billing & Reporting**\n- Automated billing solutions (mentioned on the doctors use-case page)\n- Performance reporting within EHR\n- Clinical Quality Measures (CQMs) — certified for (c)(1), with specific CQMs for pediatric weight/nutrition counseling and diabetes HbA1c monitoring\n- Value-based care program support\n\n**Integrations & Interoperability**\n- FHIR R4 API (certified (g)(10))\n- HL7 connectors\n- Integration with existing EMR systems (marketed as a feature for enterprise tier)\n- Auth0 for authentication\n- Change Healthcare / Optum Clinician integration\n\n**Security & Administration**\n- HIPAA and SOC 2 compliant infrastructure\n- Role-based access control\n- Multi-factor authentication\n- Audit logging, automatic logoff, encryption (certified (d) criteria)\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on certified criteria and vendor descriptions, Careexpand stores and manages the following data:\n\n**Clinical data** (evidenced by certifications and feature descriptions):\n- Patient demographics (a)(5)\n- Medication orders/CPOE data (a)(1)\n- Implantable device lists (a)(14)\n- Care plans (b)(11)\n- Clinical notes and encounter documentation (described in EHR features)\n- Problem lists, medication lists, allergy lists (implied by C-CDA transitions of care (b)(1))\n- Lab orders (described in e-prescribing/lab features)\n- Prescription data (e-prescribing feature)\n- Clinical quality measure data (c)(1)\n\n**Telemedicine/communication data** (described in features):\n- Video/phone consultation records\n- Multi-channel messages between providers and patients\n- Patient portal communications\n- Direct messaging (h)(1)\n\n**RPM data** (described in RPM features):\n- Remote monitoring device readings (specifics not enumerated — diabetes, hypertension, heart disease mentioned as target conditions)\n- Clinical alerts from monitoring\n\n**Administrative data** (described in practice management features):\n- Scheduling/appointment data\n- Billing data (mentioned but details thin — unclear if full claims/billing is built-in or relies on integrations)\n- Referral tracking data\n- Workflow/task management data\n\n**Security/audit data** (certified (d) criteria):\n- Authentication logs\n- Audit trails\n- Access logs\n\n**Notable gaps in clarity**:\n- The billing capability is mentioned repeatedly but never described in depth. It's unclear whether Careexpand has a full practice management billing system (claims submission, ERA/EOB processing, patient statements) or whether \"billing\" refers to simpler charge capture that relies on the Change Healthcare/Optum integration for actual claims processing. The $65/mo add-on for Change Healthcare suggests the latter.\n- RPM device specifics are not detailed — it's unclear what device types, vitals, or biometric data are actually captured and stored.\n- The website does not mention patient documents/imaging storage, faxing, or scanned document management.\n- No mention of inventory management, immunization registry reporting, or syndromic surveillance despite some products in this space offering these.\n- The distinction between what the platform stores natively vs. what flows through integrations (e.g., Change Healthcare for orders) is unclear.\n\n---\n","numLines":144,"startLine":1,"totalLines":144}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012bxvgiRLFmBq3mTBoVxiSu","type":"tool_result","content":"b10 EHI Export - CCDA\nDocument Information\n\nDocument Name: b.10 EHI Export - Patient Data via CCDA\nSpecifications\nDocument The Backend Design\nVersion: v1.0\nDescription:\n\nIntroduction\nOverview:\nThis document describes the structure and syntax of the exported Electronic Health\nInformation (EHI) as per the b.10 EHI Export requirement. It provides details on the\nexport format, file type, data structure, and instructions for accessing the data.\nObjectives:\n• Define the format and structure of exported EHI.\n• Provide a detailed data dictionary of exported elements.\n• Outline authentication and access instructions.\n\nAPI Endpoint Details\nFile Type Details\n• Format: XML\n• Schema: Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture (C-CDA) 2.1\n\n\f• Encoding: UTF-8\n• File Extension: .xml\n• Schema Reference: Based on the HL7 CDA R2 standard\n\nBasic Information\nHTTP Method: POST\nURL: /patient/:idPatient/getPatientCCDAData\nDescription: Retrieves Continuity of Care Document Architecture (CCDA) data for a specific\npatient\n\nAuthentication & Authorization\nAuthentication Required: Yes\nType: JWT Bearer Token\nGuard: JwtAuthGuard\n\nRequest Parameters\nPath Parameters\nidPatient (number): Patient ID\n\nRequest Body\nType: PatientCCDADTO\n\nData Dictionary\n\n\fThe following table provides an overview of key fields included in the exported C-CDA document:\n\nNote: Additional fields may be included depending on the data available for the patient.\n\nResponse Structure\nSuccess Response (200 OK)\n{\n\"patientData\": {\n\"demographics\": {\n\"name\": string,\n\"dob\": date,\n\"gender\": string,\n// ... other demographic fields\n},\n\"clinicalData\": {\n// Clinical information\n},\n\"monitors\": [\n// Patient monitoring data\n\n\f]\n}\n}\n\nError Responses\n401 Unauthorized\n{\n\"statusCode\": 401,\n\"message\": \"You are not Scope authorized to perform the operation\"\n}\n\n403 Forbidden","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7f660210-cc38-4b12-a559-877af036b848","uuid":"830d4667-6571-457c-80db-2f3d3c18478b","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"b10 EHI Export - CCDA\nDocument Information\n\nDocument Name: b.10 EHI Export - Patient Data via CCDA\nSpecifications\nDocument The Backend Design\nVersion: v1.0\nDescription:\n\nIntroduction\nOverview:\nThis document describes the structure and syntax of the exported Electronic Health\nInformation (EHI) as per the b.10 EHI Export requirement. It provides details on the\nexport format, file type, data structure, and instructions for accessing the data.\nObjectives:\n• Define the format and structure of exported EHI.\n• Provide a detailed data dictionary of exported elements.\n• Outline authentication and access instructions.\n\nAPI Endpoint Details\nFile Type Details\n• Format: XML\n• Schema: Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture (C-CDA) 2.1\n\n\f• Encoding: UTF-8\n• File Extension: .xml\n• Schema Reference: Based on the HL7 CDA R2 standard\n\nBasic Information\nHTTP Method: POST\nURL: /patient/:idPatient/getPatientCCDAData\nDescription: Retrieves Continuity of Care Document Architecture (CCDA) data for a specific\npatient\n\nAuthentication & Authorization\nAuthentication Required: Yes\nType: JWT Bearer Token\nGuard: JwtAuthGuard\n\nRequest Parameters\nPath Parameters\nidPatient (number): Patient ID\n\nRequest Body\nType: PatientCCDADTO\n\nData Dictionary\n\n\fThe following table provides an overview of key fields included in the exported C-CDA document:\n\nNote: Additional fields may be included depending on the data available for the patient.\n\nResponse Structure\nSuccess Response (200 OK)\n{\n\"patientData\": {\n\"demographics\": {\n\"name\": string,\n\"dob\": date,\n\"gender\": string,\n// ... other demographic fields\n},\n\"clinicalData\": {\n// Clinical information\n},\n\"monitors\": [\n// Patient monitoring data\n\n\f]\n}\n}\n\nError Responses\n401 Unauthorized\n{\n\"statusCode\": 401,\n\"message\": \"You are not Scope authorized to perform the operation\"\n}\n\n403 Forbidden","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01CwRNLW5yoYh3surDwBWPjm","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01MFFdcY4cspGkcBy1y1Ah6R","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/careexpand-llc--careexpand/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Careexpand LLC — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://bookstack.careexpandcloud.com/books/techdoc-onc-patient-ehi-export-b10/page/b10-ehi-export-ccda\n- CHPL IDs: 11625 (15.04.04.3226.Care.24.00.1.250422)\n- Certification date: 2025-04-22\n- Product: Careexpand v2024.11.0\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. **Initial probe** — HTTP HEAD request to the registered URL returned HTTP 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8`. The server runs nginx with PHP 8.3.12, powered by BookStack v24.05.4 (a wiki platform). No redirects.\n\n```bash\ncurl -sI -L \"https://bookstack.careexpandcloud.com/books/techdoc-onc-patient-ehi-export-b10/page/b10-ehi-export-ccda\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n```\n\n2. **Fetched the main page** — The page is a single BookStack wiki page titled \"b10 EHI Export - CCDA\". The content rendered fully in curl (no JavaScript required). The page contains text documentation of the EHI export API plus one embedded image containing a data dictionary table.\n\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://bookstack.careexpandcloud.com/books/techdoc-onc-patient-ehi-export-b10/page/b10-ehi-export-ccda\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o /tmp/careexpand-main.html\n```\n\n3. **Checked the parent book** — The BookStack book \"TECHDOC - ONC - Patient EHI Export - b.10\" contains exactly one page: this CCDA export page. No additional chapters or pages.\n\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://bookstack.careexpandcloud.com/books/techdoc-onc-patient-ehi-export-b10\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n```\n\n4. **Searched the entire BookStack instance** — The instance contains ~80+ books across 6 paginated result pages plus 11 shelves. This is clearly an internal development wiki. The only EHI/ONC-related book is the \"techdoc-onc-patient-ehi-export-b10\" book already found. Other books cover internal development epics (SAAS features, Dapper Care platform, DSP device monitoring, etc.), user manuals, SOPs, and third-party integrations. None contain additional EHI export documentation.\n\nNotable: The shelves page publicly exposes internal infrastructure details (RDS database hostnames, schema names for dev/staging/production environments). This is an internal wiki that was made publicly accessible — likely for ONC compliance purposes — without restricting access to only the relevant EHI export documentation.\n\n5. **Downloaded all export formats** — BookStack provides built-in HTML, PDF, Markdown, and plaintext exports. Downloaded HTML, PDF, and Markdown versions.\n\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://bookstack.careexpandcloud.com/books/techdoc-onc-patient-ehi-export-b10/page/b10-ehi-export-ccda/export/html\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o b10-ehi-export-ccda.html\ncurl -sL \"https://bookstack.careexpandcloud.com/books/techdoc-onc-patient-ehi-export-b10/page/b10-ehi-export-ccda/export/pdf\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o b10-ehi-export-ccda.pdf\ncurl -sL \"https://bookstack.careexpandcloud.com/books/techdoc-onc-patient-ehi-export-b10/page/b10-ehi-export-ccda/export/markdown\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o b10-ehi-export-ccda.md\n```\n\n6. **Downloaded the data dictionary image** — The data dictionary table is embedded as a PNG image (not HTML table). Downloaded the full-resolution version.\n\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://bookstack.careexpandcloud.com/uploads/images/gallery/2025-02/Qvqimage.png\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o data-dictionary-table.png\n```\n\n7. **Took full-page browser screenshot** for visual reference.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation consists of a **single wiki page** describing a C-CDA 2.1 XML export via an authenticated API endpoint. Here is what the documentation covers:\n\n### Export Mechanism\n- **Format**: XML conforming to C-CDA 2.1 (Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture)\n- **Endpoint**: `POST /patient/:idPatient/getPatientCCDAData`\n- **Authentication**: JWT Bearer Token with JwtAuthGuard\n- **Request body**: `PatientCCDADTO` (not further defined)\n- **Output**: A JSON response containing `patientData` with `demographics`, `clinicalData`, and `monitors` sub-objects, plus a link to download a `.xml` C-CDA file\n\n### Data Dictionary (from embedded image)\nThe data dictionary table lists 17 fields:\n\n| Field | Description | Data Type | Required |\n|-------|-------------|-----------|----------|\n| patient_name | Full name of the patient | String | Yes |\n| dob | Date of birth of the patient | Date (YYYY-MM-DD) | Yes |\n| gender | Patient's gender | String (M/F/Other) | Yes |\n| race | Race of the patient | String | No |\n| ethnicity | Ethnicity of the patient | String | No |\n| language | Preferred language of communication | String | No |\n| address | Patient's home address | String | No |\n| phone | Contact number | String | No |\n| emergency_contact | Emergency contact name and phone | String | No |\n| smoking_status | Patient's smoking habits | String | No |\n| problem_list | List of active and past medical problems | Array (Structured) | Yes |\n| medications | Active and past medications | Array (Structured) | Yes |\n| allergies | Patient allergies | Array (Structured) | Yes |\n| lab_results | Laboratory test results | Array (Structured) | No |\n| procedures | Medical procedures performed | Array (Structured) | No |\n| encounters | Clinical encounters and visits | Array (Structured) | Yes |\n| vital_signs | Blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, etc. | Array (Structured) | No |\n\nThe note states: \"Additional fields may be included depending on the data available for the patient.\"\n\n### Response Structure\nThe JSON response has three top-level objects: `demographics`, `clinicalData`, and `monitors`. The documentation shows only placeholder comments (`// ... other demographic fields`, `// Clinical information`, `// Patient monitoring data`) — no actual field definitions for `clinicalData` or `monitors`.\n\n### Access Instructions\nFour steps: authenticate with JWT, call the POST endpoint, download the returned CCDA .xml file, open in a CCDA viewer or XML library.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThe export documentation describes what is essentially a **standard C-CDA clinical summary** — the same kind of document you'd see in a (b)(1) Transitions of Care export. It covers a narrow slice of the data Careexpand stores:\n\n**Clearly covered (by the data dictionary):**\n- Demographics (name, DOB, gender, race, ethnicity, language, address, phone, emergency contact)\n- Problem lists\n- Medications\n- Allergies\n- Lab results\n- Procedures\n- Encounters\n- Vital signs\n- Smoking status\n\n**Clearly missing or not mentioned:**\n- **Billing data** — No mention of charges, claims, payments, superbills, or any financial data. The product research indicates Careexpand has billing/practice management capabilities (at the $249/mo tier) including a billing dashboard and superbills. None of this appears in the export.\n- **Care plans** — Despite being certified for (b)(11) care plans, the export data dictionary does not include care plan data.\n- **Prescriptions / e-prescribing data** — The export lists \"medications\" but not prescription details (prescriber, pharmacy, fill status, SIG). The product supports AI-assisted e-prescribing.\n- **Referrals** — The product has automated referral management, but referral data is absent from the export.\n- **Clinical notes / encounter documentation** — The product markets \"clinical documentation with AI-assisted automated coding\" but the export has no note text, progress notes, H&P, or narrative documentation fields.\n- **Telemedicine records** — Video/phone consultation records, virtual visit data. The product's core offering is telemedicine. None of this appears.\n- **Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) data** — The response JSON hints at a `monitors` array, but the data dictionary doesn't document what it contains. RPM is a significant product feature (device readings for diabetes, hypertension, heart disease).\n- **Patient portal communications** — Messages between providers and patients.\n- **Immunization records** — Not mentioned.\n- **Implantable devices** — Despite being certified for (a)(14) implantable device lists, this data is absent from the export.\n- **Images/documents/attachments** — Not mentioned.\n- **Intake forms** — The product has customizable intake forms; none appear in the export.\n- **Custom/specialty clinical data** — AI-generated metatags, protocol data, gaps-in-care assessments.\n\n**This is a classic (b)(10) vs (g)(10) confusion.** The export is a C-CDA document — the same format used for transitions of care under (b)(1) and the same clinical data classes available through the FHIR API under (g)(10). It covers roughly the USCDI core data elements and nothing more. A true (b)(10) export should include *all* electronic health information in the designated record set, which for Careexpand would include billing records, telemedicine session data, RPM readings, care plans, referrals, clinical notes, e-prescribing details, and any other patient-specific data stored in the system.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Format**: C-CDA 2.1 XML — a well-established HL7 standard\n- **Appropriateness**: C-CDA is appropriate for clinical summary data (the subset it covers). However, C-CDA cannot represent billing data, RPM device readings, telemedicine session metadata, or many of the other data types Careexpand stores. A true (b)(10) export would need a supplementary format (CSV, JSON, database dump) for data that doesn't fit C-CDA.\n- **The \"Array (Structured)\" data types** in the dictionary are not further defined. There is no documentation of the internal structure of problem_list entries, medication entries, encounter entries, etc. A developer receiving a C-CDA file could parse it using standard C-CDA tooling, but the documentation itself doesn't explain what template IDs, code systems, or value sets Careexpand uses.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Very poor.** This is minimal, compliance-checkbox documentation:\n\n- **Single page**: The entire EHI export documentation is one wiki page (~4 printed pages in PDF).\n- **Data dictionary is an image**: The key data dictionary table is embedded as a PNG screenshot, not as structured text. This is not machine-readable and cannot be queried.\n- **No field-level detail for structured arrays**: The 7 \"Array (Structured)\" fields (problem_list, medications, allergies, lab_results, procedures, encounters, vital_signs) have no sub-field documentation. What fields does a medication entry contain? What coding systems are used? Unknown.\n- **Response structure is a placeholder**: The JSON example uses comments (`// Clinical information`) instead of actual field definitions.\n- **PatientCCDADTO is undefined**: The request body type is referenced but never documented.\n- **No sample data or example files**: No example C-CDA output, no sample XML.\n- **No schema files**: No XSD, no Schematron, no profile definitions.\n- **No worked examples**: No step-by-step walkthrough of making an actual export request.\n- **Ambiguous output format**: The documentation describes a JSON response structure but says the export format is C-CDA XML. It's unclear whether the JSON response *contains* the C-CDA data inline, returns a download link, or wraps the C-CDA in a JSON envelope.\n\nA developer could not implement an import of this data based solely on this documentation. They would need to call the API and reverse-engineer the actual output.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Table-name level at best. The 17 fields listed are top-level data categories, not a true field-level dictionary. No column data types beyond \"String\" and \"Array (Structured)\".\n- **Value sets**: No coded fields are documented with value sets. Gender is listed as \"String (M/F/Other)\" but no code system. No ICD, SNOMED, RxNorm, LOINC, or CPT references.\n- **Relationships**: No entity relationships documented.\n- **Versioning**: Document says \"Version: v1.0\". BookStack shows Revision #5, created/updated 1 year ago by \"Ameya\" (matches the CHPL contact Ameya Parab, Chief Software Strategist).\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://bookstack.careexpandcloud.com/books/techdoc-onc-patient-ehi-export-b10/page/b10-ehi-export-ccda\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (content renders via curl; browser used for screenshot only)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n\n- **No obstacles** — the URL worked immediately, no authentication required, no JavaScript rendering needed.\n- **Data dictionary as image** — The data dictionary table is embedded as a PNG image rather than an HTML table, making it non-machine-readable. The BookStack Markdown export includes the image link but not the table data as text.\n- **Internal wiki exposure** — The BookStack instance is an internal development wiki with ~80+ books covering internal development, infrastructure credentials, and other sensitive information all publicly accessible. This suggests the vendor made their entire internal wiki public rather than creating a dedicated public-facing documentation page for EHI export compliance.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":375,"cache_read_input_tokens":58121,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":375},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7f660210-cc38-4b12-a559-877af036b848","uuid":"f3aedaa0-75f1-495f-90d9-21f017d42d0c"}

patient | Date (YYYY-MM-DD) | Yes |\n| gender | Patient's gender | String (M/F/Other) | Yes |\n| race | Race of the patient | String | No |\n| ethnicity | Ethnicity of the patient | String | No |\n| language | Preferred language of communication | String | No |\n| address | Patient's home address | String | No |\n| phone | Contact number | String | No |\n| emergency_contact | Emergency contact name and phone | String | No |\n| smoking_status | Patient's smoking habits | String | No |\n| problem_list | List of active and past medical problems | Array (Structured) | Yes |\n| medications | Active and past medications | Array (Structured) | Yes |\n| allergies | Patient allergies | Array (Structured) | Yes |\n| lab_results | Laboratory test results | Array (Structured) | No |\n| procedures | Medical procedures performed | Array (Structured) | No |\n| encounters | Clinical encounters and visits | Array (Structured) | Yes |\n| vital_signs | Blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, etc. | Array (Structured) | No |\n\nThe note states: \"Additional fields may be included depending on the data available for the patient.\"\n\n### Response Structure\nThe JSON response has three top-level objects: `demographics`, `clinicalData`, and `monitors`. The documentation shows only placeholder comments (`// ... other demographic fields`, `// Clinical information`, `// Patient monitoring data`) — no actual field definitions for `clinicalData` or `monitors`.\n\n### Access Instructions\nFour steps: authenticate with JWT, call the POST endpoint, download the returned CCDA .xml file, open in a CCDA viewer or XML library.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThe export documentation describes what is essentially a **standard C-CDA clinical summary** — the same kind of document you'd see in a (b)(1) Transitions of Care export. It covers a narrow slice of the data Careexpand stores:\n\n**Clearly covered (by the data dictionary):**\n- Demographics (name, DOB, gender, race, ethnicity, language, address, phone, emergency contact)\n- Problem lists\n- Medications\n- Allergies\n- Lab results\n- Procedures\n- Encounters\n- Vital signs\n- Smoking status\n\n**Clearly missing or not mentioned:**\n- **Billing data** — No mention of charges, claims, payments, superbills, or any financial data. The product research indicates Careexpand has billing/practice management capabilities (at the $249/mo tier) including a billing dashboard and superbills. None of this appears in the export.\n- **Care plans** — Despite being certified for (b)(11) care plans, the export data dictionary does not include care plan data.\n- **Prescriptions / e-prescribing data** — The export lists \"medications\" but not prescription details (prescriber, pharmacy, fill status, SIG). The product supports AI-assisted e-prescribing.\n- **Referrals** — The product has automated referral management, but referral data is absent from the export.\n- **Clinical notes / encounter documentation** — The product markets \"clinical documentation with AI-assisted automated coding\" but the export has no note text, progress notes, H&P, or narrative documentation fields.\n- **Telemedicine records** — Video/phone consultation records, virtual visit data. The product's core offering is telemedicine. None of this appears.\n- **Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) data** — The response JSON hints at a `monitors` array, but the data dictionary doesn't document what it contains. RPM is a significant product feature (device readings for diabetes, hypertension, heart disease).\n- **Patient portal communications** — Messages between providers and patients.\n- **Immunization records** — Not mentioned.\n- **Implantable devices** — Despite being certified for (a)(14) implantable device lists, this data is absent from the export.\n- **Images/documents/attachments** — Not mentioned.\n- **Intake forms** — The product has customizable intake forms; none appear in the export.\n- **Custom/specialty clinical data** — AI-generated metatags, protocol data, gaps-in-care assessments.\n\n**This is a classic (b)(10) vs (g)(10) confusion.** The export is a C-CDA document — the same format used for transitions of care under (b)(1) and the same clinical data classes available through the FHIR API under (g)(10). It covers roughly the USCDI core data elements and nothing more. A true (b)(10) export should include *all* electronic health information in the designated record set, which for Careexpand would include billing records, telemedicine session data, RPM readings, care plans, referrals, clinical notes, e-prescribing details, and any other patient-specific data stored in the system.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **Format**: C-CDA 2.1 XML — a well-established HL7 standard\n- **Appropriateness**: C-CDA is appropriate for clinical summary data (the subset it covers). However, C-CDA cannot represent billing data, RPM device readings, telemedicine session metadata, or many of the other data types Careexpand stores. A true (b)(10) export would need a supplementary format (CSV, JSON, database dump) for data that doesn't fit C-CDA.\n- **The \"Array (Structured)\" data types** in the dictionary are not further defined. There is no documentation of the internal structure of problem_list entries, medication entries, encounter entries, etc. A developer receiving a C-CDA file could parse it using standard C-CDA tooling, but the documentation itself doesn't explain what template IDs, code systems, or value sets Careexpand uses.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Very poor.** This is minimal, compliance-checkbox documentation:\n\n- **Single page**: The entire EHI export documentation is one wiki page (~4 printed pages in PDF).\n- **Data dictionary is an image**: The key data dictionary table is embedded as a PNG screenshot, not as structured text. This is not machine-readable and cannot be queried.\n- **No field-level detail for structured arrays**: The 7 \"Array (Structured)\" fields (problem_list, medications, allergies, lab_results, procedures, encounters, vital_signs) have no sub-field documentation. What fields does a medication entry contain? What coding systems are used? Unknown.\n- **Response structure is a placeholder**: The JSON example uses comments (`// Clinical information`) instead of actual field definitions.\n- **PatientCCDADTO is undefined**: The request body type is referenced but never documented.\n- **No sample data or example files**: No example C-CDA output, no sample XML.\n- **No schema files**: No XSD, no Schematron, no profile definitions.\n- **No worked examples**: No step-by-step walkthrough of making an actual export request.\n- **Ambiguous output format**: The documentation describes a JSON response structure but says the export format is C-CDA XML. It's unclear whether the JSON response *contains* the C-CDA data inline, returns a download link, or wraps the C-CDA in a JSON envelope.\n\nA developer could not implement an import of this data based solely on this documentation. They would need to call the API and reverse-engineer the actual output.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Table-name level at best. The 17 fields listed are top-level data categories, not a true field-level dictionary. No column data types beyond \"String\" and \"Array (Structured)\".\n- **Value sets**: No coded fields are documented with value sets. Gender is listed as \"String (M/F/Other)\" but no code system. No ICD, SNOMED, RxNorm, LOINC, or CPT references.\n- **Relationships**: No entity relationships documented.\n- **Versioning**: Document says \"Version: v1.0\". BookStack shows Revision #5, created/updated 1 year ago by \"Ameya\" (matches the CHPL contact Ameya Parab, Chief Software Strategist).\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://bookstack.careexpandcloud.com/books/techdoc-onc-patient-ehi-export-b10/page/b10-ehi-export-ccda\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (content renders via curl; browser used for screenshot only)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n\n- **No obstacles** — the URL worked immediately, no authentication required, no JavaScript rendering needed.\n- **Data dictionary as image** — The data dictionary table is embedded as a PNG image rather than an HTML table, making it non-machine-readable. The BookStack Markdown export includes the image link but not the table data as text.\n- **Internal wiki exposure** — The BookStack instance is an internal development wiki with ~80+ books covering internal development, infrastructure credentials, and other sensitive information all publicly accessible. This suggests the vendor made their entire internal wiki public rather than creating a dedicated public-facing documentation page for EHI export compliance.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}
